scope: 25 exact historical keys outside other assignments; full old operators and endpoint scopes inspected. Full source page 334 re-read for the fiscal classification, effectiveness and social-base argument.

rows.review_disposition: 809CB preserves the Royal Session as the first concrete attempt to reverse the new sovereignty in Doyle’s 297 discussion. Keep the historical definition and actual June scope; do not extend one failed reversal to every later form of resistance.

8EB/B64AD must retain Artois’s role in the Île d’Yeu expedition and failure to reach mainland forces. Correct departure/recall evidence to 313; broad biographical pages cannot substitute for the actual episode.

Reject alternative_to between Egyptian strategy and its naval defeat: the Nile was a later reversal, not a competing proposal. DA4B must preserve the alternative to direct invasion, speculative India logic and separately sourced strategic failure, with 332–333 insufficient for the later battle by themselves.

B319 can internalize renewed indirect taxation as fiscal reconstruction. Full 334 confirms the listed levies, rejected salt tax, revenue rationale and slow results; preserve the source’s own classification rather than silently replacing it from outside knowledge.

CB77 must retain property as the asserted basis of political competence and the restricted second-stage electoral colleges. Broad male-taxpayer primary voting was not the same electorate that chose legislators.

032D can internalize the 1793 constitution as the immediate step toward deeper change, plus bread, national lands under Ventôse and punishment in the printed plan. Do not reduce the entire programme to property abolition.

B319 must retain the return of unpopular indirect taxes as a source-identified reversal of revolutionary principle on 334. An abstract abandoned-principles endpoint is unnecessary once that explicit contrast remains.
23ECC correctly reverses accelerated_by: Varennes accelerated emigration and militarization. Preserve earlier waves and differing motives so the flight does not become the sole cause of exile.

Retire the broad Mirabeau/later-electoral-monarchy association. His earlier constitutional counsel and the contingent later electoral alternative are distinct episodes, not a direct causal continuity proved by 299–300.

2A89 must preserve Pichegru’s documented dealings and their use to justify claims of imminent restoration. Retire the abstract target while explicitly distinguishing his treason from an unproved conspiracy by the whole elected majority.

F4D/B319 must retain the contradiction between propertied ideology and bankruptcy/tax burdens alienating creditors and taxpayers. Full 334 directly supports this; an unresolved social-base label is not reason to drop the argument.

733FB must retain Grégoire’s constitutional Church, continued Sunday observance and resistance to décadi/deist alternatives. These are evidence of limits to policy, not merely the existence of a new cult.

F4D’s analogy with 1793 can include renewed clerical coercion, while 5B270 retains specific oath, liability and actual deportation distinctions. Retire the synthesis edge without asserting institutional identity between periods.

733FB can internalize promotion of Theophilanthropy as an alternative to Catholicism, with official favour and poor popular response. Do not preserve normalized supports as if the policy achieved replacement.

7593 must retain Valmy’s aftermath as a turning point, with Condé’s survival in 4F5D and later routes separately dated. Do not assign the whole 1792 collapse to Quiberon or Louis XVIII merely through broad historical projection.

4D74 preserves dependence on foreign powers and their independent aims. Specific British/Condé/Quiberon episodes are separate facets; preserve their differences without multiplying an undifferentiated dependency across every mapped parent.

Louis XVI’s participation in Varennes belongs directly in 621651. Mirabeau’s earlier counsel and Louis XVIII’s later role are not equivalent; remove the latter projection and do not claim contrast edge 69A alone preserves participation.

2E013 can retain the 1796 mission as part of the peace-negotiation sequence, with genuine British willingness and French delay. This does not license copying Pitt’s entire earlier coalition/colonial programme into Lille.

DA4B can internalize obstacles to direct invasion leading to the Egyptian alternative. Preserve Dutch naval loss, ports, Hoche’s death and continued anti-British purpose, while avoiding a single-cause account.

0364 must retain Carnot/Barthélemy’s pragmatic accommodation versus the triumvirs’ fears, with Barras’s initial wavering. Accommodation is not proof of royalist treason, nor were the triumvirs a timeless fixed bloc.

56435 can internalize conservative section dominance enabling Vendémiaire organization. Preserve the post-Prairial change and limited representativeness, not an assertion that all Paris supported the rising.

677352/33CF can retain different constitutional monarchist positions and later electoral possibilities. Retire the generic related edge without equating all exiles with either pures or one limited-monarchy design.

F4D can retain Fructidor as a founding coup in the subsequent authoritarian pattern, with 48B’s concrete mechanisms and 29CD’s later Floréal separately dated. Retire a repeated includes edge, not the sequence.
032D must preserve Babeuf’s initial tactical disagreement and later reconciliation under persecution on 325. Do not project this 1796 development solely onto 3F2B’s 1799 resurgence.

As for the preceding row, the early Jacobin revival/reconciliation belongs with 032D and 4E189’s contemporary distress, not only the later 1799 parent. Retire an unbound revival label with chronology and internal division retained.
